channel.title: Joel Seignior — writing
channel.description: Essays and field notes on commercial law, legal AI tooling, and knowledge work in major-project delivery, by Joel Seignior in Melbourne.

item.title: The Org Chart Is Now an Architecture Diagram
item.description: What a small legal AI paper says about how AI-native firms should be wired, and what happens when the agents disagree.

item.title: The Stack You Didn’t Choose
item.description: A field guide for in-house lawyers buying legal AI — or having it bought for them.

item.title: I Let an AI Build My Research Library. Then It Invented a Law That Didn’t Exist.
item.description: How a weekend experiment grew into a knowledge pipeline that fact-checks itself — and what it taught me about using AI for serious work.

item.title: Tokenomics: Why the Cost of Legal AI Is Quietly Rising
item.description: For two years the question was whether legal AI could do the work. In 2026 a second question has caught up: what does the work cost to run?

item.title: Keep your reference knowledge in flat Markdown
item.description: A worked example from Victorian construction law — on what makes a portable reference pack genuinely portable, and the discipline plain text imposes.
